item.title: Un nuevo análisis forense concluye que Jeffrey Epstein no se suicidó: fue homicidio por estrangulamiento
item.description: Para el experto forense Michael Freeman, hay muchos misterios alrededor de la muerte de Jeffrey Epstein . Pero para él, contra la visión oficial, lo que no es un misterio es que el financiero pedófilo no se quitó la vida en 2019 en una celda de Nueva York, a pocos meses de su esperado juicio. Tras haber estudiado durante meses la autopsia y las imágenes del cadáver de Epstein, su conclusión es que la causa más probable de muerte fue el homicidio. No se quitó la vida ahorcándose, sino que murió estrangulado por detrás. Su determinación vuelve a agitar el fantasma de Epstein, un asunto que… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.

item.title: Van Gogh Auction Challenge: Heirs seek to halt Sotheby’s sale; auction house disputes duress
item.description: Descendants of German publisher Samuel Fischer have requested Sotheby’s to withdraw a Van Gogh painting from auction. They argue the painting's sale in 1936 resulted from Nazi persecution and associated pressures. Samuel Fischer acquired the artwork in 1909, and it changed hands under questionable circumstances after his death. Sotheby’s claims there is no evidence of duress in the sale, but they are engaging with the family. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: ‘Spared a lot’: Kessler twins explained assisted dying decision in final letter
item.description: Pop-singing sisters, who died aged 89 last year, described their declining health and desire to depart life together Alice and Ellen Kessler, the identical pop-singing twins who chose to jointly end their lives through assisted dying last year, said they had “reached rock bottom” due to health problems and had been relieved to be able to die together. The German sisters, who became huge television stars in the 1960s and 70s, especially in Italy and the US, said a catalogue of health conditions had left them with no desire to carry on living.
